'''Lyndon Neal Smith''' (born 26 December 1964) is an English academic who is Professor in Computer Simulation and Machine Vision at the School of Engineering at the [[University of the West of England]]. He is also Director of the Centre for Machine Vision at the [[Bristol Robotics Laboratory]].

== Early life ==
Smith was born in [[Stroud]], [[Gloucestershire]], on 26 December 1964 to Lionel Alfred Smith and Dorothy Smith. He received a [[Bachelor of Science]] (BSc) from the [[University of Wales]] in 1986, a [[Master of Science]] (MSc) from the [[Cranfield Institute of Technology]] in 1988, and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) from the [[University of the West of England]] in 1997.<ref>{{Cite book|date=2001|title=Who's Who in Science and Engineering: 2002-2003|isbn=0837957605|publisher=Marquis Who's Who; 6th edition|page=906}}</ref> His PhD thesis was entitled ''A knowledge based system for powder metallurgy technology''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?did=1&uin=uk.bl.ethos.364080 |title=A knowledge based system for powder metallurgy technology |work=British Library EthOS |access-date=14 October 2023}}</ref> He completed a secondment at the [[Pennsylvania State University]] which lasted for a year.<ref>{{Cite journal |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0166361505001296 |title=Dynamic photometric stereo for on line quality control of ceramic tiles |year=2005 |journal=Computers in Industry |doi=10.1016/j.compind.2005.05.017 |access-date=23 June 2020 |last1=Farooq |first1=A. R. |last2=Smith |first2=M. L. |last3=Smith |first3=L. N. |last4=Midha |first4=P. S. |volume=56 |issue=8–9 |pages=918–934|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Career ==
Smith is Professor in Computer Simulation and Machine Vision at the School of Engineering at the [[University of the West of England]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.uwe.ac.uk/Person/LyndonSmith|title=Professor Lyndon Smith|work=UWE Bristol|access-date=23 June 2020}}</ref> He is also Director of the Centre for Machine Vision at the [[Bristol Robotics Laboratory]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uwe.ac.uk/research/centres-and-groups/machine-vision/members |title=Members of the Centre for Machine Vision (CMV) |work=UWE Bristol |date=5 October 2023 |access-date=14 October 2023}}</ref>

He has developed a technique for the simulation of the packing densities of particles with irregular morphologies.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0927025697000037#!|title=Computer simulation of morphology and packing behaviour of irregular particles, for predicting apparent powder densities|year=1997 |journal=Computational Materials Science|doi=10.1016/S0927-0256(97)00003-7 |access-date=5 August 2020|last1=Smith |first1=L. N. |last2=Midha |first2=P. S. |volume=7 |issue=4 |pages=377–383 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He helped develop 3D face recognition technology which he said was "on the verge of becoming really big" in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mercia.co.uk/news-media/news/2017/jun/26/3d-facial-recognition-technology-on-the-brink-of-c/|title=3D facial recognition technology on the brink of commercial breakthrough|work=Mercia|date=26 June 2017|access-date=23 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bristol247.com/news-and-features/news/uwe-lead-way-3d-facial-recognition-tech/|title=UWE leads the way in 3D facial recognition tech|website=bristol247.com|date=19 June 2017|access-date=23 June 2020}}</ref>

Smith has been involved in plans to replace [[turnstile]]s on the [[London Underground]] with a facial recognition system.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/videos/world/2018/02/09/you-are-your-password-great-by-design-lon-orig.cnn|title=You are your password: The world of biometrics|work=CNN|date=12 February 2018|access-date=23 June 2020}}</ref> He said that facial recognition technology under development could replace train tickets, and have applications in stores, train stations and banks.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/mach/tech/how-facial-recognition-systems-will-reshape-your-daily-life-ncna801336|title=How Facial Recognition Systems Will Reshape Your Daily Life|work=NBC News|last=Baggaley|first=Kate|date=14 September 2017|access-date=23 June 2020}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Smith has lived in [[Wedmore]], [[Somerset]],<ref>{{cite news |date=1 December 2020 |title=FREE DOWNLOAD !! Wedmore Professor – Latest Book Now Available |url=https://www.theisleofwedmore.net/news/wedmore-professor-latest-book-now-available/ |work=The Isle of Wedmore |access-date=14 October 2023}}</ref> for over 18 years, and formerly served as a member of Wedmore Parish Council. His hobbies include listening to [[British classical music]] and [[light music]], as well as painting.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lyndon Smith |url=https://wedmore-pc.gov.uk/council-members/lyndon-smith/ |work=Wedmore Parish Council |access-date=11 October 2026 |archive-date=14 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250614082959/https://wedmore-pc.gov.uk/council-members/lyndon-smith/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>
